title: Lalita's city of walls
hookLine: Lalita's city of walls, and why worship greets every guardian first
carry: greet every guardian on the way to the center
tomorrow: a trampled garland, and the gods lose their shine. what left?
last: A WHOLE HOUSE GATHERED TO ONE POINT.

lines: A PINCH OF RED, AT THE EDGE.
cards: The Purana that tells Lalita's story describes her city, Sri Nagara, raised for her by the gods' architect, Vishvakarma, and the builder Maya. Wall inside wall, ring inside ring, each with its guardians.

Past the last wall stands a palace of wish-granting gems, Chintamani, and at its heart, her throne. Her thousand names remember it: ruler of the auspicious city, the one who dwells inside the house of gems.
No one walks straight to her. A guest crosses every ring and greets each guardian. Now a home, centuries later.
A ghee lamp just lit, a brass plate of red kumkum, a grandmother at her Sri Yantra. She takes a pinch of powder and reaches, not for the center, but for the outer edge.

teach.b: Sri Vidya reads the yantra as a map of that city.
Each layer is an avarana, an enclosure, and the worship called avarana puja walks them in order: the square, the circles, the lotuses, the triangles, and only at the end, the bindu.
At each enclosure, the goddesses said to guard it are honored by name. This isn't only Sri Vidya. The same order shapes worship in many Hindu temples.

teach.h: GANESHA, THE DOORKEEPERS, THEN THE SHRINE.
teach.b: At a temple, people greet Ganesha first, bow to the doorkeepers carved at the entrance, the dvarapalas, and often circle the shrine before they reach the inner room.
Many temples keep a whole family of smaller shrines around the main one.
The teaching: the holy has a household, and you honor the household on the way in. Arriving at God isn't a grab; it's a greeting, layer by layer.

teach.h: ONE NAME, ONE PINCH OF KUMKUM.
teach.b: A simpler form lives in many homes: kumkum archana, a pinch of red offered for each of Lalita's names. One name, one pinch, the red slowly gathering. Here the senses teach.

teach.h: GREET EVERY GUARDIAN ON THE WAY IN.
teach.b: Powder between the fingers, the smell of the lamp, names said one after another: the body learns the order before the mind can explain it. Edge first. Center last.

how: In Sri Vidya avarana worship the yantra's enclosures are honored in order from the outer square to the bindu; at temples, many Hindus greet Ganesha and the doorkeepers before the inner shrine; in many homes people offer kumkum while reciting the Lalita Sahasranama, one pinch for each name.

o: a map of a palace's courtyards used on festival days
a city of walls, worshipped layer by layer, edge to center
a pattern of red powder drawn fresh at each doorway

games.q: the walk inward — tap the pairs.
p: a pinch of red for each name

s: Hindu worship goes straight to the central shrine
Ganesha, the doorkeepers and the smaller shrines are often greeted first: the same order as the avarana puja.
Lalita's names call her the ruler of the auspicious city
Sri Nagara, wall within wall, her throne at the heart.
the kumkum offering with her names can happen only in a temple
in many homes, people offer a pinch for each name.

games.q: you're helping at a friend's family puja and your first instinct is to take your flowers straight to the yantra's center. what does the avarana order suggest?
o: start at the outer square and greet each layer on the way in.
go straight to the center, since that's where the Goddess sits.
stay at the edge; the center is never offered anything at all.
games.why: like a guest crossing Lalita's city, the worship greets each enclosure's guardians and arrives at the bindu last. temples work the same way: Ganesha and the doorkeepers first.

practice: Gather a few small things: flowers, grains of rice, or nothing but your fingertips. Set them down, or touch the table, in a ring, one at a time and slowly, the way kumkum is offered with each name.
With each one, say a holy name you love, or, if you don't pray, simply: i greet you. Then place the last one in the middle, and rest there.

wordCard.voice: The Sri Yantra in worship: its avaranas, the enclosures, honored one by one from the edge to the center.

orig.note: Sanskrit avarana, an enclosure or covering: each layer of the yantra.

carryVoice: Keep this: greet every guardian on the way to the center. A guest crosses every courtyard. Day sixteen thirty-five.

sources.ref: Lalita Sahasranama, the names Shrimannagaranayika (ruler of the auspicious city) and Chintamanigrihantastha (dwelling within the house of wish-gems)
